phases.name: Phase 1 · Protected mobility and symptom control
phases.focus: Maintain protection of the repaired tendon while addressing pain, guarding, and restricted mobility.
phases.interventions: Conventional care: education on protocol and activity modification; gentle, pain-limited passive or assisted shoulder flexion and external rotation only within surgeon-set limits; scapular mobility/control, posture, and permitted distal-joint motion. No forceful stretching or resisted cuff work unless specifically authorized.

phases.name: Phase 2 · Controlled motion and early motor control
phases.focus: Progress motion and introduce low-load neuromuscular control only if healing stage and protocol permit.
phases.interventions: Conventional care remains primary; progress assisted toward active motion within protocol, add gentle scapular setting and functional movement practice. Two sessions may use appropriately supported Redcord for low-load, pain-free movement/control if cleared; avoid traction, high effort, or positions that load the repair. Defer strengthening if not authorized.

phases.name: Phase 3 · Reassessment and progression planning
phases.focus: Reassess response and set the next progression based on protocol, objective change, and function.
phases.interventions: Conventional reassessment of pain, flexion, external rotation, and permitted strength/function; update home program and work/activity guidance. Progress active motion or light strengthening only with appropriate surgeon clearance and satisfactory response. No shockwave planned.

short_term_goals: Within 4 weeks, improve right shoulder flexion from 85° active/110° passive to at least 110° active and 125° passive, if permitted by the surgeon’s protocol, without a sustained increase in pain.

long_term_goals: Within approximately 10–14 weeks, or the surgeon-approved rehabilitation stage, progress toward right shoulder flexion of 150° and external rotation of 45°, measured consistently and without compensatory movement.
Within approximately 12–16 weeks or when strengthening is cleared, progress right shoulder flexor and external-rotator strength toward 4+/5 without pain escalation or loss of motion.
Progress toward pain-free sleep and a graded return to work-related lifting, with load and overhead demands advanced only when cleared and tolerated.
precautions: Follow the operating surgeon’s protocol as the controlling plan; verify restrictions before progressing passive, assisted, active, or resisted motion. The supplied history places the patient at approximately 8 weeks post-op, but exact timing and repair-specific limits must be confirmed.
Protect the repair: avoid forceful end-range stretching, sudden reaching, heavy lifting, pushing/pulling, unsupported overhead activity, and resisted cuff loading until specifically cleared.
Keep exercise discomfort mild and transient; reduce range/load or stop if pain sharply increases, symptoms persist or worsen into the following day, or motion deteriorates.
Do not use shockwave over or near the healing repair unless explicitly approved by the surgeon; it is not planned in this episode.
Seek medical advice for new marked swelling, redness/heat, fever, sudden loss of function, new numbness/tingling, or severe/unremitting pain.
home_program: 1. Supported pendulum (only if permitted): 1–2 sets of 30–60 seconds, 1–2 times daily; let the arm relax and make small, gentle movements.
2. Supine assisted shoulder flexion with the uninvolved hand or a stick (within prescribed range): 2 sets of 8–10, once daily; move slowly and do not force the end range.
3. Assisted external rotation with elbow supported at the side (within prescribed limit): 2 sets of 8–10, once daily; stop at gentle tension, not pain.
4. Scapular setting in comfortable posture: 2 sets of 8–10 with 3–5 second holds, once daily; draw shoulder blade gently back/down without shrugging.
5. Elbow, wrist, and hand active range of motion: 1–2 sets of 10–15, once or twice daily; keep the shoulder relaxed and supported. Perform only exercises allowed by the surgeon’s protocol.
review_points: Before or at session 1: obtain the operative date, protocol, restrictions, and clearance for active motion/strengthening; clarify external-rotation measurement method.
After session 3: review pain response, sleep, adherence, and any symptom flare; maintain or modify range and exercise dose.
At the end of week 2: repeat flexion and external-rotation measures (record active/passive status), verify protocol-based progression, and decide whether Redcord is appropriate.
At session 10: reassess ROM, pain, permitted strength and functional tolerance; compare with baseline and agree on next phase or surgeon follow-up if progress is limited.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Protect and restore mobility
phases.focus: Manage symptoms, maintain safe mobility, and begin progressive weight bearing and activation.
phases.interventions: Conventional therapy: education, symptom-guided ankle range of motion, gait and weight-bearing progression, gentle strengthening, and balance initiation. Use Redcord in selected sessions for supported, low-load movement if tolerated. No shockwave planned; it is not a routine first-line intervention for an acute grade II ankle sprain.

phases.name: Phase 2 · Strength, balance, and function
phases.focus: Progress strength, proprioception, and functional loading toward usual activities.
phases.interventions: Conventional therapy: progressive calf and ankle strengthening, single-leg balance, step and gait tasks, and graded functional practice. Use Redcord in selected sessions for controlled neuromuscular training as appropriate. Advance only if pain, swelling, and movement quality remain acceptable.

short_term_goals: By session 3, demonstrate an independent symptom-management and home-exercise routine, with exercises performed without a meaningful increase in pain or swelling.
By session 6, show improved ankle mobility and tolerate progressively increased weight bearing and walking, as measured against first-session findings.
By session 6, perform basic supported single-leg balance and ankle strengthening with good control and no symptom flare.
long_term_goals: By session 10, walk on level ground for at least 30 minutes, or the patient's agreed equivalent activity, without a limp and without a significant increase in pain or swelling.
By session 10, demonstrate functional ankle strength and balance sufficient for the patient's agreed daily or recreational tasks, with safe movement control.
Independently continue a graded home program and understand criteria for progressing or reducing activity.
precautions: Use pain and swelling response to guide loading; reduce intensity if symptoms notably worsen during exercise or remain elevated afterward.
Avoid aggressive inversion stress and high-impact or cutting activity until gait, strength, balance, and symptom response support progression.
Use appropriate support and assistive devices if needed for safe weight bearing; reassess if walking tolerance declines.
Seek medical reassessment for inability to bear weight, marked or worsening swelling/pain, bony tenderness, numbness, skin color or temperature changes, or failure to improve as expected.
home_program: 1. Ankle pumps and comfortable ankle circles — 2 sets of 10 each direction, 3–5 times daily; stay in a comfortable range.
2. Ankle alphabet — 1 round, 1–2 times daily; trace small, controlled letters without forcing painful motion.
3. Isometric ankle eversion and inversion — 5 repetitions of 10-second holds each direction, once daily; press gently into the hand or a fixed surface.
4. Seated or standing calf raises — 2 sets of 10, once daily as tolerated; use hand support and keep the movement controlled.
5. Supported single-leg balance — 3 holds of 20 seconds, once daily when safe; keep a stable surface within reach and stop if balance or symptoms deteriorate.
review_points: Session 1: Record pain, swelling, ankle range of motion, strength, gait, weight-bearing tolerance, balance, and patient-specific activity goals; screen for associated injury.
After session 3: Check symptom response, home-program adherence, gait, and early mobility; modify load or arrange reassessment if progress is limited.
Around session 6: Recheck mobility, strength, balance, and walking tolerance; determine readiness for more demanding functional tasks.
Session 10: Compare findings with baseline, review goal attainment and remaining limitations, and agree on self-management, continued progression, or further evaluation.
